candidate.answerReason: Three copies of 3³ give 3 × 3³, which is a product of four factors of 3 and equals 3⁴.

methods.label: Three equal addends
methods.explanation:
The sum contains three equal addends, so it is three times \(3^3\). Expanding the power shows how many factors of \(3\) this gives:
\[\begin{aligned}3^3+3^3+3^3&=3\cdot3^3\\&=3\cdot(3\cdot3\cdot3)\\&=3^4=81.\end{aligned}\]
The answer is \(3^4\), choice \(\mathrm A\).
methods.levelReason: Uses repeated addition as multiplication and the definition of a positive integer power.
